sources.title: A First Course in Causal Inference
sources.author: Peng Ding
sources.page_mapping: Printed pages are physical minus26 in these sections.
sources.scope: Finite complete-randomization assignment moments, exact difference-in-means variance and expected Neyman variance; independent stratified weighted variance; separate superpopulation versus randomization perspectives. Prior accepted v05-c12 sharp-null rank scope physical51–55/printed25–29 is reused honestly.
cautions: The finite-population CLT is stated rather than proved in the inspected section; it is not inherited as a proved theorem. A nondegenerate normalized variance and a specified triangular-array condition would be essential.

A conservative asymptotic variance does not imply a realized estimate always exceeds true variance or exact finite-sample coverage. A limit at nominal coverage alone also does not establish eventual finite coverage above nominal.
Terminology for CRE in the later superpopulation section includes independent assignment. Our chapter distinguishes fixed treatment count from independent Bernoulli assignment.

sources.title: Estimating average causal effects under general interference, with application to a social network experiment
sources.version: arXiv1305.6156v4,20June2018, as identified on retrieved body/metadata; journal reference2017 is separate
sources.scope: Known randomization distribution and exposure mapping; individual and joint exposure probabilities; positive support and correctly specified exposure-level potential outcomes; HT mean unbiasedness and finite covariance expansion.
cautions: An exposure label must map equal labels to equal potential outcomes across assignments; merely calculating a network label does not validate it.
Positive marginal exposure probabilities identify that target mean but do not guarantee all joint probabilities are positive or all contrast variance terms are observable.
General asymptotic inference, later refinements and empirical results are outside inspected/proved scope.

sources.version: CEPR Discussion Paper6059,January2007 cover on inspected92-page primary PDF; not final handbook pagination
sources.page_mapping: Printed page numbers are physical minus4 in inspected sections.
sources.scope: Design/power tradeoffs, group assignment and independent cluster information, compliance and attrition; equal response rates need not remove selection bias.
cautions: Power quantile expressions in this source are planning approximations. Our original known-Gaussian example derives both tails exactly; no unknown-variance exact t power is inherited.
Distinguish standard-error multiplier sqrt(1+(m-1)rho) from variance multiplier1+(m-1)rho; rho is the common-component share, not the idiosyncratic variance share.
Displayed group-count formula scales as inverse square root of J with critical values held fixed; the adjacent roughly proportional wording must not be copied literally.
Increasing compliance strengthens the assignment contrast under fixed local effect; its inverse enters a detectable local effect. Do not reverse that direction.
Basic bounded-outcome attrition intervals here are original population identification bounds, not the more restrictive monotonicity/rank-based trimming bounds discussed later in the source.
No historical application, general multiarm allocation claim or source exercise is adopted as our own evidence.
